label: Late original / <DEL> steps of sequences that begin with two of {c,l,2,k,w,3,q,o,v}
explanation: Fires only during the input part of the sequence (original steps t>=3 and the <DEL> step), never during the copy phase. The <DEL> step holds 62% of activation mass (7.4% of <DEL> steps fire). It looks like a context unit set by the first original tokens. It is strongest when the sequence starts with c, l or 2 (first_tok lift 5-6x), and k, w, 3, q, o, v also push it up. Within such sequences it fires on first-occurrence input tokens (in_first=1 carries 97% of mass), and more often on j, r, u, g than on h, b, 0. The largest activations (0.95-1.0 of max) are at <DEL> after openings like c c, l c c, c c l. It does not fire at t<=2, in the copy phase, or on repeated input tokens. The response behaves like a graded, roughly additive score over the opening tokens, so a boolean predicate gets mass recall around 0.8 but low precision (~0.3): many sequences with qualifying openings stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+6.25), orig0=l (+5.65), orig0=2 (+5.63), orig1=c (+4.82), orig0=w (+4.10), orig0=3 (+4.10). Lower it: phase=2 (-9.30), prev3_tok=- (-6.87), in_tok=c (-5.01), in_tok=l (-4.80).
